notes.label: Source
notes.text: Sheet 2: CS Field Filter; exact filter Direct CS / AI; 26 entries, 2 duplicates -> 24 unique programmes.

notes.label: Scope
notes.text: All 24 unique programmes retained, including excluded / unknown funding so none silently disappear.

notes.label: Priority 1
notes.text: Best topical fit (not a prediction of acceptance or funding).

notes.label: Priority 3
notes.text: Lower fit, funding problem, or discontinued.

notes.label: Admission type
notes.text: Single apply means apply via programme/consortium portal; no independent application to each mobility university generally required.

notes.label: Two links
notes.text: Course/admission link = programme details; Erasmus Apply = programme application gateway. No separate EU-wide Erasmus scholarship portal.

notes.label: Stipend
notes.text: €1,400/month is standard full EMJM award; only available if a funded scholarship is actually awarded. For unknown-funded calls this is conditional, not guaranteed.

notes.label: Pakistan Eligible
notes.text: Yes means nationality permitted in published admission rules; selection, nationality caps and degree equivalence still apply. Unknown means unverified.

notes.label: MOI
notes.text: MOI waiver policy is degree-country-specific at some programmes. A Pakistani English-taught degree does NOT grant automatic IELTS exemption.

notes.label: GRE
notes.text: Not required / not listed means no GRE mandate identified in examined admission material; verify when 2027 call documents publish.

notes.label: Date filter
notes.text: Confirmed window: IPCVai, EDISS, CoDaS, MULTICOM, NeuroData, CYBERSURE, AISS, plus month-only CDE/EMILDAI. DEAI opened October 20.

notes.label: Status
notes.text: Unannounced is not the same as ineligible; no scholarship is not the same as no admission.

notes.label: Sources
notes.text: Each programme has official links in columns L, M and P.

items.title: Image Processing and Computer Vision ai
items.countries: France / Spain / Hungary (verify mobility track)
items.moi: YES: university certificate for entire English-taught bachelor
suggestions: Computer vision, deep learning and linear algebra
items.fee_detail: Self-funded participation costs: €4,500 per year for EU students and €9,000 per year for non-EU students (two-year programme, so about €18,000 for non-EU). The intake year isn't stated on the page. A 2025 self-funded round also offered a half fee waiver. The programme's own site (ipcv.eu) was unreachable during research, so this is from partner university PPKE's application page.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Programme on the Engineering of Data-intensive Intelligent Software Systems
items.countries: Year 1: Finland → Year 2: (specialization partner country varies by track)
items.moi: NO for Pakistan bachelor alone; specified countries only
items.fee_detail: Participation costs are €9,000 per year (€18,000 over the two years) for students from all countries (intake 6, 2026–28). The EMJM scholarship and the EDISS scholarship each include a full waiver of participation costs. Earlier intakes (1–4) listed €4,500/yr for programme-country and €9,000/yr for partner-country students.

items.title: Communications Engineering and Data Science
items.countries: Home university: (Finland / France / Portugal / Germany / Spain) → host university in another partner country
items.moi: NO general Pakistan MOI waiver; see permitted methods
suggestions: Explain interest in communications plus ML
items.fee_detail: The programme fee is €8,000 per academic year and is the same for all students regardless of citizenship. The Erasmus Mundus scholarship covers the programme fee for the normal duration of studies, plus €1,400/month for up to 24 months.

items.title: Data Engineering and Artificial Intelligence
items.countries: Belgium → Spain → (Austria or France or Italy) → thesis host varies
items.moi: Check official exemption; do not assume Pakistani MOI
suggestions: Strong coding, maths and data engineering
items.fee_detail: Self-funded students pay €4,500 per academic year (Programme-country) or €9,000 per academic year (Partner-country). Full and partial DEAI scholarships cover 100% of participation costs; self-funded students pay them. The intake year isn't stated.

items.title: Data Science of Human Multimodal Communication: European and International Joint Masters Degree
items.countries: Spain → Sweden → Germany (thesis location flexible)
items.moi: Pakistani MOI alone not sufficient per published exemption

alerts.label: MULTICOM scholarship
alerts.text: FAQ says one application and automatic scholarship consideration; a different financial-aid page mentions a separate aid filing. Follow live application instructions.

items.fee_detail: Self-funded students pay public prices set jointly by the three degree-awarding institutions and revised yearly. Current estimate: €17,000 per year, €34,000 for the full programme. Scholarships cover participation costs (tuition, insurance, admin and cultural costs); candidates may be offered a full scholarship, partial funding or none. No EU/non-EU split is given.

items.title: International Master in Brain and Data Science
items.countries: Israel → Portugal / Italy / Netherlands / Finland; summer school Croatia
items.ielts: Mandatory test listed; exact IELTS band verify
items.moi: Possible: official university certificate if all teaching English (FAQ conflicts with call)

alerts.label: NeuroData English
alerts.text: Application call says English test mandatory, while FAQ allows a fully English-taught university certificate: verify with consortium before relying on MOI.

items.fee_detail: The official costs page shows its fee table as an image that could not be read; a third-party listing (Mastersportal) shows about €10,000 per year for international students, which is unverified. Important, from the official page: from the 2027 intake only self-funded students will be accepted until EU refunding is obtained, and each edition has only 5 self-funded places. Self-funded students may get a first-year tuition waiver and a local monthly scholarship of about €740, depending on availability.

items.title: Master's Programme in Cybersecurity and Assurance
items.countries: Norway → Finland / Sweden / Denmark / Estonia / France / Austria
items.fee_detail: The official Scholarships & fees page has a 'Self-Financed Students' tab, but its amounts aren't in the page text that could be read, so open it directly. The '16,800 EUR / year' on that page is the scholarship grant (12 × €1,400), not a fee. 2026 intake: up to 18 scholarships; the 2027 intake application deadline is 4 January 2027 (EURECOM).

items.title: Sustainable Information Technologies for Societies Joint Masters
items.countries: Estonia → Finland / Portugal (path per programme)
items.stipend: €1,400/mo if full EMJM award; verify 2027 availability
items.moi: Verify specific exemption on admissions page
items.call_status: Opens in window; scholarship terms verify
items.fee_detail: Self-funded fee: €2,000 per semester, €8,000 for the four semesters. No separate EU/non-EU fee is listed. The Erasmus Mundus scholarship includes tuition coverage plus a €1,400 monthly contribution.

items.title: Copernicus Master in Digital Earth
items.countries: Austria → (France or Czechia) → thesis host flexible
items.call_status: Opens in window (month only); funding verify
items.fee_detail: The official costs page is script-rendered and could not be read. Search snippets from the official site say selected self-funded candidates receive a participation-cost fee waiver (classes, exams, graduation) but still pay their own travel, visa, accommodation, living costs and the Austrian student union fee; the same snippets mention regular partner tuition of about €2,000 per semester (€8,000 total) with a higher partner-country figure, and estimate €30,000–32,000 for 24 months including living costs. No application fee. Confirm the details on the site.

items.title: European Master in Law, Data and Artificial Intelligence
items.countries: Netherlands / Ireland / Italy / Finland / Brazil (track-dependent; exact route varies by intake)
items.stipend: 2027 full stipend NOT confirmed; 2026 partial awards only
items.call_status: Opens in window (month only); full funding unverified
items.fee_detail: From a search snapshot of the official fee page (2026–2028 intake): €20,919 per year for non-EU and €10,424 for EU self-funded students, with a €500 deposit deducted from first-year fees. An older 2024 brochure listed €19,908 non-EU. The fee page is behind a bot check, so it could not be opened directly; confirm on the site. The Erasmus+ Master Degree Loan is limited to residents of programme countries.

items.title: European Master in Linguistic Data Science
items.countries: Ireland / Portugal / Italy / Spain (several mobility paths; sequence varies)
items.stipend: €1,400/mo if full EMJM award; 15 awards announced
items.moi: YES: full English-taught degree with MOI certificate
items.fee_detail: Tuition for the full four-semester programme is €18,000 and can be paid in instalments; no EU/non-EU split is stated. EMJM scholarship holders are exempt from tuition fees (15 scholarships for the 2027–2029 cohort).

items.title: Master of Science in Geospatial Technologies
items.countries: Germany / Spain / Portugal (three-campus consortium; sequence varies by study plan)
items.call_status: Open; opening date and funding unverified
items.fee_detail: Tuition is €1,800 per semester (4 semesters = €7,200); the page gives no EU/non-EU split or academic year, and it also quotes 2023-era visa figures, so it may not be current. The 2027 EMJM scholarship covers tuition of €1,800/semester plus €1,400/month for 18 months; grant holders cover all other costs.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Cybersecurity
items.countries: Finland / Sweden / Italy / Spain (track-dependent; sequence varies)
suggestions: Relaunch/eligibility not confirmed; older Pakistan restriction
items.fee_detail: The annual registration fee is €4,500, including international health and accident insurance; students without a scholarship or fee waiver pay it, and no separate EU/non-EU rate is listed. Scholarship holders get €1,400/month for the 24 months plus a fee waiver; fee-waiver-only awards also exist. The page that could be read is for the 2025 intake (it said 6 scholarships had already gone to Pakistan in that call), so check the 2027 call.

items.title: Educating software engineers with a sustainability mindset to improve the well-being of people through software solutions
items.countries: (Finland / Sweden / Germany; two study periods in two countries, path varies)
items.fee_detail: €4,500 per year for Programme Country students and €9,000 per year for Partner Country students; no separate self-funded rate is listed. Heads-up: the programme page says there will be no new intakes (it is being renewed as SE4GD+) and aims to open to self-funded applicants in 2026. Scholarship holders have tuition covered.

items.title: Functional Advanced Materials Engineering with Artificial Intelligence for Sustainability
items.countries: Year 1: (France or Germany) → Year 2: (France / Germany / Belgium / Portugal), in a different country
suggestions: Materials science + AI; needs chemistry/physics background
items.fee_detail: Self-funded tuition is €4,000 per year for the EU Member States plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, North Macedonia, Serbia and Turkey, and €9,000 per year for all other countries (this includes Pakistan). Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders have tuition covered plus €1,400/month for up to 24 months (only for students who have never had Erasmus Mundus funding). The intake year isn't stated.

items.title: European Master in Embedded Computing Systems
items.countries: Germany / Norway / United Kingdom (route depends on university choice)
items.fee_detail: From a search summary of the official EMECS admission page: European students €4,000 per year (€8,000 total) and non-European students €8,000 per year (€16,000 total). The same page reportedly says EMECS did not admit new students for Fall 2025, and some listings say the Kaiserslautern campus charges no tuition at all, so confirm before applying. The university's server refused the connection, so the page could not be opened.

items.title: Master of Applied Cybersecurity
items.countries: Turkey → (Germany or North Macedonia)
items.fee_detail: Secondary listings give about €5,175 for self-funded students, but they disagree on whether that is the total (Mastersportal shows €2,587 per year over 24 months) or per year. The official site (cybermacs.eu) returned a server error, so none of this is verified.

items.title: Big Data Management and Analytics
items.countries: See programme mobility page
suggestions: Big data, database systems, distributed computing
items.fee_detail: Tuition is €9,000 per year for Partner Country students and €4,500 per year for Programme Country students, including national enrolment fees and insurance (TU/e specialisation fees may be higher for non-EU Programme Country students). The page doesn't name an intake. Heads-up: the programme says its current European Commission funding has finished, applications for the 2024–2026 grant period are closed, and a news item says the next application period 'starts soon'.

items.title: Mathematical Modelling, Simulation and Data Science for Industrial and Societal Challenges
items.countries: Country route depends on specialization; verify current mobility pathway
items.fee_detail: No published tuition figure was found for self-funded students. The site says scholarship holders (€1,400/month for 24 months) do not pay fees, and that a tuition fee waiver scheme exists at one partner for selected non-EU students; self-funded places go to reserve-list applicants. Ask the coordinators for the self-funded fee.

items.title: System-level, sustainable, and artificial intelligence-aided structural design
items.countries: See programme mobility page
items.fee_detail: No official website or published fee was found for S3AID; the sheet's link is only the generic EU project search. Check the programme once it publishes its call.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in Advanced Microscopy with Artificial Intelligence
items.countries: See programme mobility page
items.fee_detail: The programme site could not be read (it rate-limited requests) and no published fee was found; the only independent source describes MICROSCOM as a newly funded Erasmus Mundus master. Check microscom.eu for the call.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master In Artificial Intelligence
items.countries: Spain / Italy / Netherlands / Slovenia (track-based; sequence varies)
items.stipend: NO published 2027 full EMJM round (self-funded call)
suggestions: Do not assume stipend in self-funded round
items.fee_detail: From a search summary of the official UPF page (2026–2028 cohort): self-funded students pay €9,000 per year in tuition, EU students get a 50% discount (€4,500), and everyone covers their own travel and living costs. UPF estimates €1,000–1,500 per month living costs. The UPF page returned an access error when opened directly, so please confirm on the site.

items.title: ChEMoinformaticsplus - Artificial Intelligence in Chemistry
items.countries: France + partner country (varies by track)
items.fee_detail: All accepted students are exempt from tuition fees, with or without a scholarship. But the page states that recruitment of the 2027–2029 intake will be without scholarship, and applicants who reach the interview stage must explain how they will fund their mobility (for example through alternative grants).

items.title: Master's programme in Security and Cloud Computing
items.countries: Finland → Year 2: specialization partner country varies
items.fee_detail: Participation cost is €9,000 per year for students from partner countries and €3,000 per year for programme-country students. Heads-up: the page says SECCLO will not have any new student intakes; the fees and scholarship information refer to the last admission round (intake 2024). Erasmus Mundus scholarships contribute the participation cost, plus separate travel and subsistence amounts.
